t: This is Wulfstan Street, in Hammersmith and Fulham. It is named after Wulfstan, who became Bishop of London in 996. In 1002 he was elected to both Worcester and York, held the two together until 1016, then stayed Archbishop of York until he died in 1023. He is remembered as a writer of sermons. In 1014 he wrote his most famous work, a homily he called the Sermo Lupi ad Anglos, the Sermon of the Wolf to the English.
